verdict.rationale: Plaid's Workflow Management editor lets users set conditional rules inside a verification template. For example, it can run an extra check only when another check fails or the session looks high-risk, or route by the user's country, and it does this through a no-code editor. That is a real built-in rule-to-action capability, but it only covers which verification checks run within a session. Webhooks send events outward rather than letting users define automated actions. missing for 10: general event-triggered actions beyond check sequencing (e.g., auto-approve/reject, routing, notifications on STATUS_UPDATED), documented rule-builder depth and limits, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: even run certain checks conditionally, such as only running a particular verification if another verification fails or indicates a high-risk session, or running different checks based on your user's country of origin
No-code editor to create and change verification flows
